title: Kashmir Shaivism opening (the Shiva Sutras)
hook: a run of short lines in the Shiva Sutras turns the self into a dancer, the inner self into a stage, and the senses into the audience

segments.voice: Yesterday, in our Kashmir Shaivism opening, a thread of the Shiva Sutras said wonder marks the stages of yoga. A new week starts in the same book.
screen: `THE SHIVA SUTRAS.` · `A NEW WEEK, THE SAME BOOK.`

segments.voice: On a lit stage, one dancer becomes a lover, then a king, then a frightened deer, then a god. The face changes, the hands change, and it's the same dancer the whole time. The Shiva Sutras turn that picture inward in three very short lines. Nartaka atma: the self is a dancer. The stage is the inner self. The spectators are the senses. A theater, built in three breaths. Some days back, Nataraja danced in bronze, in a ring of fire. Here the dance moves indoors.
screen: `ONE DANCER, MANY ROLES.` → `NARTAKA ATMA.` → `A THEATER, INDOORS.`

segments.voice: Start with the dancer. In Kashmir Shaivism, there is one consciousness, and it's Shiva's. On this view, everything a person is, is that consciousness playing a part: a worker, a parent, a worried person at a red light. It plays each one fully. Then the stage: the inner self, the antaratma. The play doesn't happen out there somewhere. It happens on the floor of your own awareness, where thoughts and moods step out and take a bow. Then the audience: the senses. Your eyes, your ears, your skin sit in the seats and watch the show. Commentators in the tradition read the three lines together as a description of someone who has woken up. Not someone who quits the roles. Someone who plays all of them and never forgets who's dancing. The anger at a coworker still comes on stage. So does the tenderness toward a child. But the one in the costume knows it's a costume. A dancer who forgets gets lost in the part. A dancer who remembers can play a tragedy all evening and walk home whole. Not to stop the dance. To dance it awake.
screen: `THE SELF IS A DANCER.` · `THE STAGE IS THE INNER SELF.` · `THE SENSES ARE THE AUDIENCE.` · `PLAYING A PART, AWAKE.` · then, large: `NEVER FORGET WHO'S DANCING.`

segments.voice: Name a few roles you've already played today: the one who got up, the one who answered a message, the one who was short with someone, or kind. Let each one step onto the inner stage, take its bow and step off, and notice the one who's watching, who was there for every role. If you pray, you can offer the whole performance to Shiva.
Kashmir Shaivism opening, the Shiva Sutras. Today's lines: the self is a dancer, the stage is the inner self, the spectators are the senses.
Your line: Kashmir Shaivism opening, the Shiva Sutras. The one in the costume knows it's a costume. See you tomorrow.
